```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

Purpose: the project has used a plain merged (not integrated) Seurat object
throughout, on the basis of an earlier visual-only check (PCA/UMAP coloured
by `orig.ident` in `02-initial_QC.Rmd`) that batch effects weren't an issue.
Sophie is now asking questions about transitions within the mesenchyme, so
before looking at that we're revisiting whether integration changes the
picture. Batch is defined here as **sequencing run** (E11.5 vs E12.5 - the
two stages were sequenced separately), not individual sample, per discussion
2026-10-21.

This does NOT replace `final_interesting_cells_0.6.rds` - it produces a
separate, comparable object with the same clustering parameters (dims = 30,
resolution = 0.6, matching `06.1-cellType_filter.Rmd`) so the two can be
compared side by side before deciding whether integration should become the
new baseline.

# Clean-up environment

```{r clean-up}
rm(list = ls(all.names = TRUE)) # will clear all objects including hidden objects
gc() # free up memory and report the memory usage
options(max.print = .Machine$integer.max,
        scipen = 999,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
        dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE)
set.seed(42) # set seed for reproducibility
```

# Load libraries

```{r}
# Core tidyverse
library(tidyverse)
library(tibble)
library(dplyr)

# Core single cell
library(Seurat)
library(harmony)

# additional plotting functions
library(patchwork)
```

# Set project directories

```{r}
project_repo_dir <- "/home/melanie-smith/workDir/sophieWiszniak/20251104_sophieWiszniak_ncc_pa"
data_dir <- file.path(project_repo_dir, "outDir", "06-cluster_marker_genes")
out_dir  <- file.path(project_repo_dir, "outDir", "06.5-harmony_batch_integration_check")

if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) {
  dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}
```

# Load the full merged object

- Same object used by every `07.x`/`08.x` script - post-QC, post-filtering,
  single joined `RNA` layer across all 4 samples, clustered at resolution
  0.6 (30 PCs) in `06.1-cellType_filter.Rmd`.

```{r}
re_embed_interesting_cells <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, "final_interesting_cells_0.6.rds"))
stopifnot(inherits(re_embed_interesting_cells, "Seurat"))

DefaultAssay(re_embed_interesting_cells) <- "RNA"

# sanity check: batch variable (sequencing run = stage)
table(re_embed_interesting_cells$stage, re_embed_interesting_cells$orig.ident)
```

# Re-split the RNA layer by sequencing run (stage)

- `IntegrateLayers()` requires per-batch split layers. The object currently
  has a single joined layer (`JoinLayers()` was called when it was first
  merged in `02-initial_QC.Rmd`), so split it back out by `stage`
  (e11 vs e12 = the two sequencing runs).

```{r}
re_embed_interesting_cells[["RNA"]] <- split(
  re_embed_interesting_cells[["RNA"]],
  f = re_embed_interesting_cells$stage
)

# confirm the split worked - should see per-stage layers now
re_embed_interesting_cells[["RNA"]]
```

# Pre-integration processing

- Same `LogNormalize` approach used throughout this project (no SCTransform
  anywhere in the pipeline) - `NormalizeData -> FindVariableFeatures ->
  ScaleData -> RunPCA`, run on the split-layer object as Seurat v5's
  integration workflow expects.

```{r pre-integration-processing}
re_embed_interesting_cells <- NormalizeData(re_embed_interesting_cells)
re_embed_interesting_cells <- FindVariableFeatures(re_embed_interesting_cells)
re_embed_interesting_cells <- ScaleData(re_embed_interesting_cells)
re_embed_interesting_cells <- RunPCA(re_embed_interesting_cells)
```

# Harmony integration

```{r harmony-integration}
re_embed_interesting_cells <- IntegrateLayers(
  object         = re_embed_interesting_cells,
  method         = HarmonyIntegration,
  orig.reduction = "pca",
  new.reduction  = "harmony",
  verbose        = FALSE
)

# re-join layers after integration
re_embed_interesting_cells[["RNA"]] <- JoinLayers(re_embed_interesting_cells[["RNA"]])
```

# Cluster and embed on the Harmony-corrected space

- Same `dims`/resolution as the original clustering (`06.1-cellType_filter.Rmd`:
  `dims = 1:30`, `resolution = 0.6`) for a fair before/after comparison.
  Stored under new names so the original `umap`/`seurat_clusters` used
  everywhere downstream are left untouched.

```{r cluster-harmony}
re_embed_interesting_cells <- FindNeighbors(re_embed_interesting_cells, reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:30)
re_embed_interesting_cells <- FindClusters(re_embed_interesting_cells, resolution = 0.6, cluster.name = "harmony_clusters")
re_embed_interesting_cells <- RunUMAP(re_embed_interesting_cells, reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:30, reduction.name = "umap.harmony")
```

# Save the integrated object

```{r}
saveRDS(
  re_embed_interesting_cells,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "final_interesting_cells_0.6_harmony_integrated.rds")
)
```

# Compare: original merge vs Harmony integration

## UMAP coloured by sequencing run (stage) - the batch-mixing check

```{r compare-batch-mixing, fig.width=14, fig.height=6}
p1 <- DimPlot(re_embed_interesting_cells,
              reduction = "umap",
              group.by = "stage",
              shuffle = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Original (merged, not integrated)")

p2 <- DimPlot(re_embed_interesting_cells,
              reduction = "umap.harmony",
              group.by = "stage",
              shuffle = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Harmony-integrated")

p_batch <- p1 + p2
ggsave(
  plot = p_batch,
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "compare_umap_by_stage.png"),
  width = 14, height = 6
)
p_batch
```

## UMAP coloured by cell type - did biology survive integration?

```{r compare-celltypes, fig.width=14, fig.height=6}
p3 <- DimPlot(re_embed_interesting_cells,
              reduction = "umap",
              group.by = "new_celltypes",
              shuffle = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Original - cell type")

p4 <- DimPlot(re_embed_interesting_cells,
              reduction = "umap.harmony",
              group.by = "new_celltypes",
              shuffle = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Harmony-integrated - cell type")

p_celltype <- p3 + p4
ggsave(
  plot = p_celltype,
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "compare_umap_by_celltype.png"),
  width = 14, height = 6
)
p_celltype
```

## UMAP coloured by genotype

```{r compare-genotype, fig.width=14, fig.height=6}
p5 <- DimPlot(re_embed_interesting_cells,
              reduction = "umap",
              group.by = "genotype",
              shuffle = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Original - genotype")

p6 <- DimPlot(re_embed_interesting_cells,
              reduction = "umap.harmony",
              group.by = "genotype",
              shuffle = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Harmony-integrated - genotype")

p_genotype <- p5 + p6
ggsave(
  plot = p_genotype,
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "compare_umap_by_genotype.png"),
  width = 14, height = 6
)
p_genotype
```

## Cluster composition: original vs Harmony clusters

- Does Harmony clustering (at the same resolution) recover materially the
  same groups, or does it split/merge things differently?

```{r compare-clusters}
cluster_crosstab <- table(
  original = re_embed_interesting_cells$seurat_clusters,
  harmony  = re_embed_interesting_cells$harmony_clusters
)

cluster_crosstab

write.csv(
  as.data.frame.matrix(cluster_crosstab),
  file.path(out_dir, "cluster_crosstab_original_vs_harmony.csv")
)

# how many cells per original cell type land in each harmony cluster
celltype_harmony_crosstab <- table(
  new_celltypes   = re_embed_interesting_cells$new_celltypes,
  harmony_cluster = re_embed_interesting_cells$harmony_clusters
)

celltype_harmony_crosstab

write.csv(
  as.data.frame.matrix(celltype_harmony_crosstab),
  file.path(out_dir, "celltype_by_harmony_cluster.csv")
)
```
